title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: US stocks fell Monday (S&P 500 ~7,711, -0.4%) and futures pointed lower as Mideast tensions flared after Trump rejected Iran's latest Strait of Hormuz proposal.
Markets: Oil jumped toward $106/bbl (Brent) on Hormuz fears and Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure; gold broke below $4,200, and the 2-year Treasury yield climbed to 4.90%.

Companies: Microsoft rose ~3.7% on plans to merge its consumer and workplace Copilot AI assistants into one enterprise product; Alphabet +0.6%. Chip-equipment makers rallied (Applied Materials +2.3%, Lam Research +2.6%).
Companies: Big earnings this week - Micron, Nike and Accenture report, with Micron's own AI-driven guidance already looking conservative next to Street estimates.
Macro/Policy: Odds of an Oct. 28 Fed rate hike jumped to roughly 70%+ after hawkish comments from Governor Barr and hotter inflation data.
Macro/Policy: The Iran/Strait of Hormuz standoff and Houthi attacks are now the dominant macro risk driving oil and yields, reversing last week's optimism about a phased reopening.
